title: Swe entry domain oop fundamentals
question: Explain encapsulation, inheritance, and polymorphism in your own words, ideally with a small example of each.
idealAnswer:
Encapsulation is bundling data with the methods that operate on it and hiding internal state behind a public interface, so callers can't reach in and put the object in an invalid state

Inheritance is a class acquiring behavior and fields from a parent class, used to share common structure between related types

Polymorphism is treating objects of different concrete types through a common interface, so the same call site can invoke different behavior depending on the actual object at runtime

Gives or attempts a concrete example for at least one concept rather than only definitions, e.g. a Shape base class with Circle and Square overriding an area() method

Doesn't confuse inheritance with composition, a strong answer at least implicitly understands inheritance is an 'is-a' relationship
